subject: the want-list became books — 81 identifiers finally ingested
the_gap: build-want-list.mjs produced 81 identifiers and NO script fetched any of them. The contract said it "takes named identifiers"; nothing consumed them. A want-list nobody can act on is a list, not a pipeline.

rights_gate.rule: formal-designation, institutional-review, jurisdiction-scoped. "not-a-designation" excluded — the literal string "Public Domain License" is free text, not a designation.

the_bug_the_guard_caught.symptom: three items returned EXACTLY 170 bytes; real sizes were 200-350 KB
the_bug_the_guard_caught.actual: capturing a redirected download as a utf8 string through execFileSync truncated it; a plain retry returned the full 352,362 bytes
the_bug_the_guard_caught.fix: curl -o to a temp file with --retry 3, then rename on success
the_bug_the_guard_caught.why_it_matters: without the BAD_BODY check those three would have been written as ingested books at 170 bytes each

a_sample_that_would_have_misled_me: head -c 400 on the Donne text is pure OCR garbage — it is the scanned cover and endpapers. The first 400 bytes of a DjVuTXT file say nothing about the book. Measured across the whole file it has thousands of common English words. Quality was measured per-file over full text, not by eyeballing a prefix.
deliberately_not_done: Nothing was written to books.sqlite. Catalogue ingest is a schema-bearing write to a database six claims ground in, and belongs behind a reviewed migration. The text is on the vault with a manifest so that decision is made on evidence.
